candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 18:9-22. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Acts 3:22 (verbatim apostolic citation), Acts 7:37.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken' (Deu 18:15), Ephrem reads the prophet-like-Moses promise as the canonical Old-Testament messianic anchor cited verbatim by Peter in Acts 3:22 ('A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me') and by Stephen in Acts 7:37 — the apostolic preaching's primary Old-Testament prophecy-of-Christ proof-text alongside Ps 110:1. The 'like-Moses' qualification is fulfilled in Christ at the Transfiguration where Moses and Elijah appear with him on the mountain. Tewahedo christology cites Deu 18:15 + Acts 3:22 + the Buhe Transfiguration as the canonical triple-witness of the Mosaic-prophet identity of Christ.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

On 'The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken' (Deu 18:15), Ephrem reads the prophet-like-Moses promise as the canonical Old-Testament messianic anchor cited verbatim by Peter in Acts 3:22 ('A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me') and by Stephen in Acts 7:37 — the apostolic preaching's primary Old-Testament prophecy-of-Christ proof-text alongside Ps 110:1. The 'like-Moses' qualification is fulfilled in Christ at the Transfiguration where Moses and Elijah appear with him on the mountain. Tewahedo christology cites Deu 18:15 + Acts 3:22 + the Buhe Transfiguration as the canonical triple-witness of the Mosaic-prophet identity of Christ.
